rationales: Schwartz did not introduce the five-kingdom classification system.
Margulis contributed to biological classification but did not introduce this system.
Aristotle proposed an early classification of living things, not the five-kingdom system.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification system.
In prophase, chromosomes condense but are not yet arranged at the cell equator.
In metaphase, chromosomes align at the cell equator.
In telophase, chromosomes have reached the poles and new nuclei form.
In anaphase, sister chromatids move away from the equator toward opposite poles.
“Mala” means “bad.”
“Good” is the opposite of the meaning of “mala.”
This option is obscured and cannot be identified as the meaning.
“Water” is not the meaning of “mala.”
Lipase breaks down lipids.
Starch is broken down by amylase, not lipase.
This option is obscured and cannot be identified as lipase’s substrate.
Proteins are broken down by proteases, not lipase.
A phylum is below kingdom in the classification hierarchy.
A class is below kingdom in the classification hierarchy.
Kingdom is the largest taxon among the options.
A genus is a small taxon below family.
Stomata are openings mainly involved in gas exchange, not cytoplasmic connections between adjacent cells.
Plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells.
Lenticels are openings in woody stems that allow gas exchange.
The cuticle is a waxy protective layer and does not connect adjacent cell cytoplasm.
Microtubules are made of tubulin protein.
RNA is not the structural protein that forms microtubules.
DNA is not the structural protein that forms microtubules.
Actin protein forms microfilaments, not microtubules.
Glucose is generally converted into sucrose for transport through plants.
Sucrose is the main form in which food is transported in most plants.
Starch is an insoluble storage carbohydrate, not the usual transport form.
Lactose is a sugar found mainly in milk, not the usual plant transport sugar.
Bacteria are unicellular organisms.
A frog is a multicellular organism.
Amoeba is unicellular.
Euglena is unicellular.
Chlorophyll b is an accessory pigment rather than the main photosynthetic pigment.
Chlorophyll a is the main photosynthetic pigment.
Carotenoids are accessory pigments that absorb additional wavelengths of light.
Xanthophylls are accessory pigments within the carotenoid group.
Budding is not the process by which a sea star regrows a lost arm.
Mitosis produces the new cells needed to regenerate a lost arm.
Meiosis produces gametes rather than regenerating body parts.
Fragmentation can enable reproduction from separated pieces, but regrowth of a lost arm is regeneration by mitosis.
Leaf size can affect the surface area available for water loss by transpiration.
Higher temperature can increase the rate of transpiration.
Air movement can increase transpiration by removing moist air near the leaf.
CO₂ concentration is not generally listed as a direct environmental factor determining transpiration rate.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
Asterias rubens is a sea star, not an onion.
“Zia maiz” is not the scientific name of onion.
Felis domesticus refers to a domestic cat, not an onion.
The light reactions are not known as the S-scheme.
The sequence of electron transfers in the light reactions is called the Z-scheme.
The light reactions are not known as the L-scheme.
The light reactions are not known as the P-scheme.
Emil Fischer proposed the lock-and-key model in 1894.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model, not the lock-and-key model.
Wilhelm is not the scientist credited with proposing the lock-and-key model.
Calvin is known for work on the Calvin cycle, not the lock-and-key model.
